def decide(bars, account):
    closes = bars["close"]
    n = len(closes)
    if n < 60:
        return "HOLD", "not enough history"
    price = closes[-1]
    ma50 = sum(closes[-50:]) / 50
    regime_ok = True
    if n >= 200:
        ma200 = sum(closes[-200:]) / 200
        regime_ok = ma50 > ma200
    if account["position"] <= 0:
        if price > ma50 and regime_ok:
            return "BUY", "close above 50-day MA in uptrend regime"
    else:
        if price < ma50 * 0.98 or not regime_ok:
            return "SELL", "close below 50-day MA buffer or regime broken"
    return "HOLD", "no change"

def decide(bars, account):
    closes = bars["close"]
    n = len(closes)
    if n < 60:
        return "HOLD", "not enough history"
    price = closes[-1]
    ma50 = sum(closes[-50:]) / 50
    ma50_prev = sum(closes[-60:-10]) / 50
    slope_up = ma50 > ma50_prev
    long_ok = True
    if n >= 200:
        ma200 = sum(closes[-200:]) / 200
        long_ok = price > ma200
    uptrend = price > ma50 and slope_up and long_ok
    if account["position"] <= 0 and uptrend:
        return "BUY", "close above rising 50-day average"
    if account["position"] > 0 and not uptrend:
        return "SELL", "trend filter broken"
    return "HOLD", "no change"

Starting strategy supplied by the researcher and identical for every run; you did not write it. It is deliberately simple. Judge it on the evidence like any other version.
def decide(bars, account):
    """Seed strategy: hold the stock while its close is above the 20-day average."""
    closes = bars["close"]
    if len(closes) < 20:
        return "HOLD", "not enough history for a 20-day average"
    average = sum(closes[-20:]) / 20
    price = closes[-1]
    if account["position"] <= 0 and price > average:
        return "BUY", "close is above the 20-day average"
    if account["position"] > 0 and price < average:
        return "SELL", "close is below the 20-day average"
    return "HOLD", "no change"
